Definition: Pethachjah, the name of four Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Pethachjah is a name that appears four times in Scripture. One is the priest of the nineteenth course under David, one is a Levite named in Ezra's day, and one is a Levite who stands with the people at Nehemiah's great prayer of confession.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the name Pethachjah, whom God has freed, fits every one of them: priests and Levites freed to serve, and a people freed to confess and return.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
